title: introduce-opaque-backoff-token-and-retry-after-format-in-openai-bridge
author: Asha Menon
description: Adds a clearer, backwards-compatible retry and idempotency contract for the OpenAI compatibility layer and API gateway. This PR introduces an opaque backoff token header (X-Redwood-Backoff-Token) and normalizes Retry-After parsing to accept three canonical formats: numeric seconds, HTTP-date string, and a new 't=<unix_ts>' timestamp form in order to reduce ambiguity across clients and proxies. Also formalizes a structured error envelope field 'retry_hint' and 'backoff_token' in JSON error bodies returned by the compatibility shim and the runtime. Motivation: customers hit intermittent 429s and ambiguous retry semantics when proxying through older HTTP clients and when streaming function/tool calls; different SDKs parsed Retry-After inconsistently which caused retries to happen too early or not at all. This PR implements parsing/serialization in the API gateway, maps legacy Retry-After values to the canonical envelope in the OpenAI adapter, and surfaces an opaque backoff token that encodes server-side backoff state for more precise backoff duration estimation across retries and across routed fallbacks. The change includes: compatibility layer mapping rules, SDK-compat tests, updated end-to-end test scenarios for multiplexed streams, a migration/compatibility guide in docs, and a short deprecation timeline for legacy Retry-After-only reliance. Rollout plan: feature-flagged for two weeks, telemetry monitoring enabled for backoff-token usage, staged SDK updates recommended but server will continue to accept older Retry-After formats for 90 days. See release notes for client migration guidance.
commits: 1) gateway: parse and canonicalize Retry-After formats, emit X-Redwood-Backoff-Token in 429 responses; 2) openai-adapter: map legacy 429 payloads to structured error envelope and attach backoff token when present; 3) runtime: add token-stamping util and test harness for token expiry semantics; 4) sdk-python/compat: add parsing helpers and integration tests; 5) docs: add migration guide and examples for parsing the new envelope.
review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Please add a short note in the gateway metrics about backoff_token population rate and include a metric name to query (done in a follow-up commit).
Priya Kapoor: I requested a small refactor to separate parsing logic from header extraction so adapters can reuse (addressed in commit 3).
Liam O'Connell: Approved after we added an extra unit test to ensure RFC1123 HTTP-date parsing handles timezone variants (added).

SRE on-call: Flagged that this relies on a new datastore key for token state; we ensured token expiration is purely advisory and tokens will be ignored if store is unavailable (author responded with fallback behavior and added tests).

Author (Asha): Clarified that backoff tokens are opaque strings with HMAC to prevent tampering and include a short TTL; expanded docs to include example decoding for troubleshooting only (not recommended for clients).
release_notes: Introduce X-Redwood-Backoff-Token header and canonical Retry-After parsing. Servers will return a structured error envelope with 'code', 'message', and optional 'retry_hint' and 'backoff_token' fields. Clients should prefer 'backoff_token' when present for more accurate backoff behavior. Backwards compatibility: numeric and HTTP-date Retry-After values are still supported for 90 days; see docs/migration/retry-backoff.md for parsing examples and SDK helpers.
notes_for_ops: Feature-flag is controlled by FLAG_CANONICAL_RETRY. Telemetry added: metric redwood.backoff_token.emitted_count and redwood.retry_after.parse_errors. Monitor increase in parse_errors immediately after rollout and watch for elevated error rates upstream. If a surge is observed, roll back via the feature flag and open a postmortem.
